motion: The city should restrict car access
own_opening: Essential travel must remain possible. Restrictions should be targeted and paired with practical alternatives.
chunks: We should ban cars across the city. Cars congest streets and make walking unpleasant.
The point is to give people better public spaces. That is the proposal I want you to consider.
Let me correct the scope: I mean private cars in the downtown shopping streets during weekend afternoons only. Ambulances, disabled residents and deliveries are exempt.
checks: Acknowledges the restriction is downtown and weekend afternoons only
Does not argue that ambulances or disabled residents are banned
Offers a substantive objection to the revised restriction

motion: Schools should prohibit phones during lessons
own_claim: Targeted restrictions can preserve educational uses
own_opening: Phones can be distracting, but supervised educational uses should remain available.
chunks: A classroom phone ban improves concentration. I also claim it always raises examination scores.
Teachers need predictable rules. Constantly negotiating phone use takes time away from teaching.
I withdraw the claim about examination scores: I do not have evidence for it. My case rests only on reducing interruptions, with teacher-authorized educational use exempt.
checks: Treats the examination-score claim as withdrawn
Recognizes the educational-use exemption
Addresses classroom interruptions or predictable enforcement

own_opening: Reliable operations and adequate service matter more than a headline fare policy.
chunks: Public transport should be free for everyone because travel costs can prevent people from reaching work and school.
Making buses more accessible is a practical way to widen opportunity, especially for households under financial pressure.
To be precise, my proposal is a one-year pilot for residents below the poverty line on existing bus routes. Other riders still pay, and the pilot comes from an already allocated assistance fund.
checks: Recognizes the means-tested one-year bus pilot
Does not portray the proposal as universally eliminating all transit revenue
Raises a relevant concern such as service capacity, eligibility or evaluation

motion: Writing education remains important in the age of AI
own_claim: AI changes which writing skills deserve classroom time
own_opening: Schools should emphasize evaluating ideas and outputs rather than spending most writing time on unaided drafting.
chunks: Students should write everything themselves, because outsourcing the work weakens their ability to reason and communicate.
A student needs enough practice to recognize whether a paragraph is coherent and whether its evidence supports its conclusion.
I should narrow that: I support AI feedback and brainstorming. I require only occasional unaided drafts for assessing understanding, not a ban on AI-assisted writing.
checks: Acknowledges AI feedback and brainstorming are allowed
Does not rebut a total AI ban as the current proposal
Challenges the necessity or design of occasional unaided assessment

motion: The country should expand nuclear power
own_claim: Reliable low-carbon electricity requires multiple technologies
own_opening: Nuclear power should be considered alongside renewables where it can provide dependable low-carbon electricity.
chunks: Nuclear plants should all close immediately. Large projects can absorb money that could have funded other low-carbon options.
New construction also takes planning and careful financing, so we must compare credible alternatives rather than assume a single technology wins.
I retract the immediate-closure demand. Existing safe plants should continue operating. I oppose only new publicly subsidized reactors and propose an open comparison with renewables and storage.
checks: Distinguishes existing plants from new subsidized reactors
Does not claim the opponent demands an immediate shutdown
Responds to financing or the comparison with renewables and storage

own_claim: Some well-designed practice outside class is useful
own_opening: Brief targeted practice can consolidate skills when it does not overwhelm children or families.
chunks: Schools should reduce homework because children need time for sleep, play and family life. I have heard that reducing homework doubles attainment.
Teachers can instead use classroom time for focused practice and give families optional activities that suit their circumstances.
The doubling claim was a mistake and I withdraw it. I have no measured attainment effect. I am proposing a cap of fifteen minutes, not the abolition of reading or practice.
checks: Does not present the withdrawn doubling claim as the current evidence
Recognizes a fifteen-minute cap rather than abolition
Addresses the value or allocation of limited practice time

motion: Households should pay more for excessive water use
own_claim: Water policy should protect essential household needs
own_opening: Conservation measures must account for household size and unavoidable water needs.
chunks: We should charge higher prices to households that use a lot of water. A clear price signal can discourage waste.
People who maintain ornamental lawns during shortages should consider whether that water could be used more responsibly.
I am not proposing a surcharge on essential use. The higher rate starts only above a household-size-adjusted allowance, and documented medical needs are exempt.
checks: Recognizes household-size adjustment and medical exemption
Does not claim essential water is universally surcharged
Challenges practical measurement, threshold design or remaining distributional effects

own_claim: Work arrangements should reflect job requirements
own_opening: Teams need arrangements that preserve training, coordination and essential in-person work.
chunks: Everyone should be allowed to work remotely whenever they choose. Flexibility can reduce commuting and help employees manage responsibilities.
Trusting employees to organize their work can also shift attention from time spent at a desk to the quality of completed work.
I overstated the scope. This applies only to roles already shown to be remotely workable, with two agreed office days each week. Laboratory, clinical and on-site service roles are outside the policy.
checks: Recognizes the hybrid arrangement and role restriction
Does not argue that the policy sends clinical or laboratory work home
Discusses coordination, assessment or fairness under the revised arrangement

own_opening: New spending should demonstrate benefits relative to other essential local services.
chunks: Libraries provide a quiet place to study and access to books for people who cannot afford to buy them.
They also offer computers and help with online forms, which matters when important services expect residents to use the internet.
The proposal is to extend opening hours at existing branches and evaluate usage before considering any new buildings.
checks: Responds to access or digital assistance benefits
Recognizes extended hours at existing branches
Offers a relevant funding-priority or evaluation argument

own_opening: Dress policies should be proportionate and sensitive to what families can afford.
chunks: A common school uniform can reduce visible competition over fashionable clothing and make school rules easier to explain.
We would permit generic clothing in school colors instead of requiring a single branded supplier.
Families who cannot afford the clothes would receive vouchers. Students could adapt the uniform for religious or disability-related needs.
checks: Recognizes generic clothing and vouchers
Does not assume a compulsory expensive branded supplier
Addresses whether uniforms achieve the claimed social or administrative benefit

motion: The city should convert some parking lots into parks
own_claim: Land conversion needs local access planning
own_opening: Public space is valuable, but we must understand how each conversion affects local access and services.
chunks: Some underused municipal parking lots should become small parks. Nearby residents would gain space to sit and children would have somewhere to play.
That is the central idea: small parks in places currently occupied by underused parking. I want to emphasize the value of a place to sit and play.
The first step is a reversible trial in one lot, with access to nearby businesses monitored before any permanent conversion.
checks: Recognizes the reversible one-lot trial
Does not portray every parking lot as being permanently removed
Raises a concrete access, measurement or opportunity-cost concern

own_claim: School meal funding should target demonstrated need
own_opening: We should assess whether universal provision or targeted support better uses a limited education budget.
chunks: Free school lunches can ensure that pupils do not go hungry in the middle of the school day and can remove stigma associated with separate assistance programs.
To repeat my main concern, no child should spend lessons hungry. I am stressing access to lunch and avoiding stigma.
The plan is universal lunches within participating schools, funded by replacing existing meal subsidies rather than taking money from classroom teaching.
checks: Addresses access or stigma
Recognizes the stated funding source
Does not assert as fact that the plan directly cuts classroom budgets

own_opening: A citizen should be able to abstain without being treated as endorsing any candidate.
chunks: Compulsory voting can encourage political participation. However, by compulsory I mean that citizens must attend or submit a ballot, and they may
leave that ballot blank or choose an explicit abstention option. Nobody would be required to endorse a candidate.
Enforcement would use a small administrative fine with exemptions for illness and other reasonable barriers, not imprisonment.
checks: Recognizes that blank ballots or abstention are allowed
Does not claim the proposal compels endorsement or imprisonment
Addresses compulsory attendance, fines or voluntary participation

motion: The city should restrict disposable plastic packaging
own_opening: Packaging policy should account for sanitation, accessibility and whether substitutes are actually suitable.
chunks: Disposable packaging creates waste that persists after its brief useful life. Restrictions should start with restaurant takeaway items, except
items needed for medical safety, disability access or food hygiene where no suitable substitute exists.
The city should phase this in over two years, publish substitution guidance and review the exemptions with affected users.
checks: Recognizes essential-use exemptions
Recognizes phased implementation
Critiques suitability, enforcement or environmental tradeoffs without treating exempt uses as banned
